accepted.s: Under the Seventh Schedule to the Constitution of India, prisons are included in which of the following?
accepted.x: Prisons are a State subject under Entry 4 of the State List in the Seventh Schedule.
accepted.tq: Test the exact List and Entry instead of relying on the general subject classification.
accepted.sec: Prison laws and prisoners' rights - Prisons Act 1894, Model Prisons Act 2023, parole/furlough, Seventh Schedule, undertrials  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the administration of prisons is correct?
o: Prisons are governed exclusively by the Union Government under the Prisons Act, 1894.
The Supreme Court directly administers all prisons through BPR&D.
Prisons are governed by the Prisons Act, 1894 and State jail manuals, while BPR&D issues advisory guidelines.
State jail manuals have no role after the enactment of the Model Prisons Act, 2023.
accepted.x: Prisons continue to be governed by the Prisons Act, 1894 and State jail manuals; BPR&D issues advisory guidelines.
accepted.tq: Identify the correct combination of governing law, State rules and advisory authority.
accepted.sec: Prison laws and prisoners' rights - Prisons Act 1894, Model Prisons Act 2023, parole/furlough, Seventh Schedule, undertrials  [other exams]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the Model Prisons Act, 2023:
1. It was prepared by the Ministry of Home Affairs.
2. It is intended to guide States in replacing the colonial Prisons Act, 1894.
3. It automatically operates as a binding Central law in every State.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The Model Prisons Act, 2023 was prepared by the Ministry of Home Affairs as a guide for States to replace the colonial 1894 Act. It is not automatically a binding Central law in every State.
accepted.tq: Separate a model guide for States from an automatically binding Central enactment.
accepted.sec: Prison laws and prisoners' rights - Prisons Act 1894, Model Prisons Act 2023, parole/furlough, Seventh Schedule, undertrials  [other exams]

accepted.s: With reference to parole and furlough, which one of the following is correct?
o: They are available only to undertrial prisoners.
They are governed by identical Central rules applicable to every State.
They are not absolute rights, and each State has its own prisoner-release rules.
They constitute an absolute constitutional right available uniformly throughout India.
accepted.x: Parole and furlough are not absolute rights. Each State frames its own prisoner-release or parole rules.
accepted.tq: Distinguish a non-absolute release facility from a uniform constitutional entitlement.
accepted.sec: Prison laws and prisoners' rights - Prisons Act 1894, Model Prisons Act 2023, parole/furlough, Seventh Schedule, undertrials  [other exams]

accepted.s: Under Section 479 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, an undertrial prisoner is generally eligible for release after undergoing which period of the maximum imprisonment prescribed, subject to the statutory conditions?
accepted.x: BNSS Section 479 provides release after one-half of the maximum term, reduced to one-third for first-time offenders, subject to the statutory conditions.
accepted.tq: Recall the paired fractions and avoid reversing the general and first-offender thresholds.
accepted.sec: Prison laws and prisoners' rights - Prisons Act 1894, Model Prisons Act 2023, parole/furlough, Seventh Schedule, undertrials  [other exams]

accepted.s: According to NCRB Prison Statistics 2024, which one of the following correctly represents the number of prisons, sanctioned capacity and inmate population respectively?
accepted.x: The reported figures were 1,333 prisons, approximately 4.53 lakh capacity and 5.11 lakh inmates.
accepted.tq: Keep the order of the three quantitative categories intact.
accepted.sec: Prison laws and prisoners' rights - Prisons Act 1894, Model Prisons Act 2023, parole/furlough, Seventh Schedule, undertrials  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which of the following statements regarding prison occupancy in India is correct?
o: The occupancy rate was 163.5%, with Delhi recording the lowest rate.
The occupancy rate was 94.6%, with Meghalaya recording the highest rate of 194.6%.
The occupancy rate was 112.7%, described as a decade-high; Delhi recorded 163.5%.
The occupancy rate was 112.7%, described as a decade-low; Delhi recorded 194.6%, the highest among the States and Union Territories mentioned.
accepted.x: Overall occupancy was 112.7%, a decade-low. Delhi recorded 194.6%, while Meghalaya recorded 163.5%.
accepted.tq: Match the overall figure with the correct high-state and location comparison.
accepted.sec: Prison laws and prisoners' rights - Prisons Act 1894, Model Prisons Act 2023, parole/furlough, Seventh Schedule, undertrials  [other exams]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding prisoners according to NCRB Prison Statistics 2024:
1. Undertrials constituted approximately 73% of inmates.
2. About 9,028 prisoners had been held for more than five years.
3. Women constituted 14.3% of inmates.
4. There were only 34 women’s prisons.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Undertrials constituted approximately 73%, 9,028 had been held over five years and there were 34 women’s prisons. Women constituted 4.14%, not 14.3%.
accepted.tq: Check each numerical statement independently, especially the altered percentage trap.
accepted.sec: Prison laws and prisoners' rights - Prisons Act 1894, Model Prisons Act 2023, parole/furlough, Seventh Schedule, undertrials  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the position of women’s prisons and States/Union Territories lacking one?
o: There were 21 women’s prisons, and 34 States/Union Territories lacked one.
There were 34 women’s prisons, and 21 States/Union Territories lacked one.
There were 34 women’s prisons, and 14 States/Union Territories lacked one.
There were 41 women’s prisons, and 21 States/Union Territories lacked one.
accepted.x: There were only 34 women’s prisons, while 21 States and Union Territories lacked a women’s prison.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the number of institutions from the number of jurisdictions without one.
accepted.sec: Prison laws and prisoners' rights - Prisons Act 1894, Model Prisons Act 2023, parole/furlough, Seventh Schedule, undertrials  [other exams]

accepted.s:
Which of the following statements correctly reflects the prison staffing and unnatural-death data mentioned for 2024?
1. Approximately 37% of posts were vacant.
2. Unnatural deaths increased by 10.7%.
3. There were 122 suicides.
4. Unnatural deaths declined by 10.7%.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Approximately 37% of posts were vacant, unnatural deaths increased by 10.7%, and 122 suicides were reported. Statement 4 reverses the trend.
accepted.tq: Reject the option that reverses the reported direction of change.
accepted.sec: Prison laws and prisoners' rights - Prisons Act 1894, Model Prisons Act 2023, parole/furlough, Seventh Schedule, undertrials  [other exams]

accepted.s: The Supreme Court’s direction concerning prisoners who had remained in custody beyond completion of their sentence related to which of the following?
o: Extension of their sentences until trial of prison officials
Automatic conversion of their sentences into parole
accepted.x: The Supreme Court ordered the immediate release of prisoners held beyond completion of their sentence.
accepted.tq: Identify the direct remedy ordered by the Court rather than an administrative consequence.
accepted.sec: Prison laws and prisoners' rights - Prisons Act 1894, Model Prisons Act 2023, parole/furlough, Seventh Schedule, undertrials  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which case is correctly matched with the constitutional status of the death penalty?
o: Bachan Singh v State of Punjab (1980) — death penalty unconstitutional
Machhi Singh v State of Punjab (1983) — abolition of capital punishment
Jagmohan Singh v State of Uttar Pradesh (1973) — death penalty constitutional
262nd Law Commission Report (2015) — death penalty constitutional for all crimes
accepted.x: In Jagmohan Singh v State of Uttar Pradesh (1973), the death penalty was held constitutional.
accepted.tq: Use the case-year-holding combination and reject swapped holdings.
accepted.sec: Death penalty - rarest of rare → case; Amnesty execution rankings  [other exams]

accepted.s: The doctrine that life imprisonment is the rule and death penalty is the exception was laid down in which case?
o: Jagmohan Singh v State of Uttar Pradesh
Machhi Singh v State of Punjab
Nilabati Behera v State of Orissa
Bachan Singh v State of Punjab
accepted.x: Bachan Singh v State of Punjab (1980) established the ‘rarest of rare’ doctrine, under which life is the rule and death is the exception.
accepted.tq: Match the distinctive doctrinal phrase with the correct case.
accepted.sec: Death penalty - rarest of rare → case; Amnesty execution rankings  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is associated with Machhi Singh v State of Punjab (1983)?
o: Categories of rarest cases and balancing aggravating and mitigating factors
Compensation for custodial death under Articles 32 and 226
Mandatory arrest safeguards for police officers
Abolition of the death penalty for all offences
accepted.x: Machhi Singh developed categories of rarest cases and required balancing aggravating and mitigating circumstances.
accepted.tq: Separate closely related death-penalty cases by their specific contribution.
accepted.sec: Death penalty - rarest of rare → case; Amnesty execution rankings  [other exams]

accepted.s: A death sentence imposed by a Sessions Court becomes executable only after confirmation by which court?
accepted.x: A death sentence passed by a Sessions Court requires confirmation by the High Court.
accepted.tq: Identify the higher authority whose confirmation is mandatory before execution.
accepted.sec: Death penalty - rarest of rare → case; Amnesty execution rankings  [other exams]

accepted.s: An appeal against a death sentence may reach the Supreme Court under which combination of constitutional provisions?
accepted.x: Appeals in such matters may lie to the Supreme Court under Articles 132, 134 and 136.
accepted.tq: Recall the exact constitutional Article cluster instead of nearby judicial provisions.
accepted.sec: Death penalty - rarest of rare → case; Amnesty execution rankings  [other exams]

accepted.s: The capital offences formerly contained in the Indian Penal Code are now located in which enactment?
o: The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, including murder under Section 479
The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, including murder under Section 103
The Protection of Human Rights Act, including murder under Section 21
The Prisons Act, 1894, including murder under Section 103
accepted.x: Capital offences formerly in the IPC now appear in the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita; murder is cited under Section 103.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the substantive criminal law from the procedural and prison laws.
accepted.sec: Death penalty - rarest of rare → case; Amnesty execution rankings  [other exams]

accepted.s: According to Amnesty International’s execution ranking referred to here, which country was identified as the world’s biggest state executioner?
accepted.x: China was identified as the world’s biggest state executioner.
accepted.tq: Test the named country directly without importing unrelated current ranking figures.
accepted.sec: Death penalty - rarest of rare → case; Amnesty execution rankings  [other exams]

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Case)
a. Nilabati Behera v State of Orissa
b. Joginder Kumar v State of Uttar Pradesh
c. D.K. Basu v State of West Bengal
d. Arnesh Kumar v State of Bihar

List-II (Principle)
i. No automatic arrest for offences punishable up to seven years
 ii. Compensation for custodial death; sovereign immunity is no defence
 iii. Arrest must be justified and a friend or relative may be informed
 iv. Mandatory arrest safeguards including arrest memo and medical examination

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Nilabati Behera concerns compensation, Joginder Kumar concerns justified arrest and informing relatives, D.K. Basu concerns arrest safeguards, and Arnesh Kumar restricts automatic arrest for offences up to seven years.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure case-principle pair and eliminate codes with swapped custodial safeguards.
accepted.sec: Custodial violence guidelines → case (D.K. Basu, Nilabati Behera, Joginder Kumar, Arnesh Kumar)

accepted.s: In which case did the Supreme Court hold that compensation under Articles 32 and 226 could be granted for custodial death and that sovereign immunity was no defence?
o: Arnesh Kumar v State of Bihar
Joginder Kumar v State of Uttar Pradesh
Nilabati Behera v State of Orissa
D.K. Basu v State of West Bengal
accepted.x: Nilabati Behera v State of Orissa (1993) recognised compensation under Articles 32 and 226 for custodial death and rejected sovereign immunity as a defence.
accepted.tq: Identify the case from its distinctive remedy and rejection of sovereign immunity.
accepted.sec: Custodial violence guidelines → case (D.K. Basu, Nilabati Behera, Joginder Kumar, Arnesh Kumar)

accepted.s: Which of the following was laid down in Joginder Kumar v State of Uttar Pradesh (1994)?
o: Every offence punishable up to seven years requires immediate arrest.
A judicial inquiry is unnecessary in every custodial death.
Arrest must be justified and not routine, and the arrestee may have a friend or relative informed.
Sovereign immunity completely bars compensation for custodial death.
accepted.x: Joginder Kumar held that arrest must be justified rather than routine and that a friend or relative of the arrestee may be informed.
accepted.tq: Reject the reversed arrest proposition and retain the specific safeguard.
accepted.sec: Custodial violence guidelines → case (D.K. Basu, Nilabati Behera, Joginder Kumar, Arnesh Kumar)

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT a mandatory safeguard associated with D.K. Basu v State of West Bengal?
o: Automatic arrest in every offence punishable up to seven years
accepted.x: D.K. Basu required safeguards such as an arrest memo, identification of officers, informing kin and medical examination. Automatic arrest for offences up to seven years is contrary to the safeguard approach associated with Arnesh Kumar.
accepted.tq: Find the one proposition that reverses the arrest-safeguard principle.
accepted.sec: Custodial violence guidelines → case (D.K. Basu, Nilabati Behera, Joginder Kumar, Arnesh Kumar)

accepted.s: Arnesh Kumar v State of Bihar (2014) is primarily associated with which proposition?
o: No automatic arrest for offences punishable up to seven years and use of a checklist
Abolition of judicial inquiry in custodial deaths
Automatic arrest for all offences punishable up to seven years
Confirmation of death sentences by the High Court
accepted.x: Arnesh Kumar restricted automatic arrest for offences punishable up to seven years and required a checklist under CrPC Section 41, now reflected in BNSS Section 35.
accepted.tq: Distinguish restriction on automatic arrest from the unrelated death-penalty procedure.
accepted.sec: Custodial violence guidelines → case (D.K. Basu, Nilabati Behera, Joginder Kumar, Arnesh Kumar)

accepted.s: Which provision makes a judicial inquiry mandatory in custodial deaths, with the corresponding current BNSS provision being Section 196?
accepted.x: CrPC Section 176(1A) made judicial inquiry mandatory in custodial deaths; the corresponding BNSS provision is Section 196.
accepted.tq: Match the old and new procedural section numbers without confusing arrest and sanction provisions.
accepted.sec: Custodial violence guidelines → case (D.K. Basu, Nilabati Behera, Joginder Kumar, Arnesh Kumar)

accepted.s: Under Section 218 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, what is required before a court takes cognisance against a public servant for acts connected with official duty?
o: Consent of the accused public servant
Approval of the National Human Rights Commission only
Confirmation by the High Court in every case
accepted.x: BNSS Section 218 requires Government sanction before courts take cognisance against public servants in the relevant circumstances, which may delay prosecution.
accepted.tq: Ask which authority must provide prior sanction before judicial cognisance.
accepted.sec: Custodial violence guidelines → case (D.K. Basu, Nilabati Behera, Joginder Kumar, Arnesh Kumar)

accepted.s:
Arrange the following States in descending order of the reported number of police-custody deaths:
A. Uttar Pradesh
B. Bihar
C. Rajasthan

Select the correct order.
accepted.x: Bihar recorded the most police-custody deaths, followed by Rajasthan and Uttar Pradesh.
accepted.tq: Use the stated ranking from highest to lower rather than alphabetical order.
accepted.sec: Custodial violence guidelines → case (D.K. Basu, Nilabati Behera, Joginder Kumar, Arnesh Kumar)

accepted.s: What was the reported relationship between police-custody deaths and convictions during 1999–2023?
accepted.x: The reported data recorded 2,253 police-custody deaths and only three convictions during 1999–2023.
accepted.tq: Pair the large denominator with the exceptionally small number of convictions.
accepted.sec: Custodial violence guidelines → case (D.K. Basu, Nilabati Behera, Joginder Kumar, Arnesh Kumar)

accepted.s: The guidelines in PUCL v State of Maharashtra (2014) concerning encounter deaths consisted of how many points?
accepted.x: PUCL v State of Maharashtra (2014) laid down 16-point guidelines for encounter deaths.
accepted.tq: Recall the exact count attached to the leading encounter-death guidelines case.
accepted.sec: Encounter deaths - PUCL vs State of Maharashtra guidelines, NHRC norms

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the PUCL guidelines on encounter deaths:
1. The tip-off should be recorded.
2. An FIR should be registered.
3. An independent investigation should be conducted by the CID or another police station.
4. An out-of-turn promotion should be granted immediately to the officers involved.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The guidelines require recording the tip-off, registering an FIR and an independent investigation by the CID or another police station. They prohibit out-of-turn promotion or a gallantry award until the officers are cleared.
accepted.tq: Spot the statement that reverses the rule on rewards before clearance.
accepted.sec: Encounter deaths - PUCL vs State of Maharashtra guidelines, NHRC norms

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT among the safeguards associated with PUCL v State of Maharashtra and encounter-death norms?
o: Granting a gallantry award before the investigation is completed
accepted.x: The guidelines require a magisterial inquiry, intimation to the NHRC or SHRC and forensic examination of weapons. Promotion or a gallantry award must not be granted until clearance.
accepted.tq: Find the prohibited reward by applying the ‘until cleared’ condition.
accepted.sec: Encounter deaths - PUCL vs State of Maharashtra guidelines, NHRC norms

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly states the position of the NHRC regarding encounter deaths?
o: They are treated as serious violations requiring mandatory reporting, post-mortem videography and independent investigation.
They can be investigated only by the armed forces.
They require only an internal police report and no post-mortem.
They are treated as routine police actions requiring no special reporting.
accepted.x: The NHRC treats encounter deaths as serious violations and requires mandatory reporting, post-mortem videography and independent investigation.
accepted.tq: Match the rights-protection body with its prescribed procedural safeguards.
accepted.sec: Encounter deaths - PUCL vs State of Maharashtra guidelines, NHRC norms

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched with a proposed way forward for reducing custodial and encounter-related abuses?
o: Tamil Nadu — withdrawal of community policing through Friends of Police
All States — replacement of independent investigation by internal inquiry
accepted.x: Body-worn cameras by the Delhi Police, Kerala’s Janamaithri Suraksha and Tamil Nadu’s Friends of Police were identified as way-forward measures, along with stronger forensic capacity.
accepted.tq: Match each institutional initiative with its correct State or police organisation.
accepted.sec: Encounter deaths - PUCL vs State of Maharashtra guidelines, NHRC norms

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes India’s status under the United Nations Convention against Torture (UNCAT)?
o: India neither signed nor ratified it and has a standalone anti-torture law.
India signed it in 1997 but has not ratified it and has no standalone anti-torture law.
India ratified it in 2010 after the Prevention of Torture Bill was enacted.
India ratified it in 1997 and enacted a standalone anti-torture law.
accepted.x: India signed UNCAT in 1997 but has not ratified it, and there is no standalone anti-torture law.
accepted.tq: Separate signing from ratification and distinguish a proposed law from an enacted one.
accepted.sec: UN Convention against Torture - India's status, Prevention of Torture Bill

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Prevention of Torture Bill, 2010 was passed by the Lok Sabha.
2. The Bill subsequently lapsed.
3. The Bill became a permanent standalone anti-torture law after being passed by the Lok Sabha.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The Prevention of Torture Bill, 2010 was passed by the Lok Sabha but later lapsed. It did not become a permanent standalone anti-torture law.
accepted.tq: Distinguish passage in one House from completion of the legislative process.
accepted.sec: UN Convention against Torture - India's status, Prevention of Torture Bill

accepted.s: The 273rd Law Commission Report recommended which of the following?
o: Replacement of the Seventh Schedule by a new prison list
Ratification of UNCAT and a draft Prevention of Torture Bill, 2017
Confirmation of all death sentences by the Supreme Court
accepted.x: The 273rd Law Commission Report (2017) recommended ratification of UNCAT and proposed a draft Prevention of Torture Bill, 2017.
accepted.tq: Match the Law Commission report number with its specific subject and recommendation.
accepted.sec: UN Convention against Torture - India's status, Prevention of Torture Bill

accepted.s: Which of the following is included among the proposed measures for strengthening India’s response to torture?
o: Withdrawing from UNCAT and removing safeguards during interrogation
Replacing forensic investigation with custodial confession
Making parole an absolute right for all prisoners
Ratifying UNCAT, enacting a standalone law and adopting the PEACE model of interviewing
accepted.x: The proposed way forward includes ratifying UNCAT, passing a standalone anti-torture law and adopting the PEACE model of interviewing.
accepted.tq: Select the option containing the complete rights-based reform package.
accepted.sec: UN Convention against Torture - India's status, Prevention of Torture Bill

accepted.s:
Match the following committees with their principal focus:

List-I (Committee)
a. Mulla Committee
b. Krishna Iyer Committee
c. Justice Amitava Roy Committee

List-II (Focus)
i. Women prisoners and greater representation of women in police
 ii. Overcrowding, undertrials, legal aid and speedy trial
 iii. National prison policy, All India Prison Service and separate undertrials

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: The Mulla Committee focused on comprehensive jail reforms, the Krishna Iyer Committee on women prisoners and women in police, and the Justice Amitava Roy Committee on overcrowding, undertrials, legal aid and speedy trial.
accepted.tq: Start with the distinctive women-prisoners focus and then eliminate the remaining mismatches.
accepted.sec: Prison reform committees → focus (Mulla, Krishna Iyer, Justice Amitava Roy)

accepted.s: Which committee recommended a national prison policy, an All India Prison Service and separate arrangements for undertrial prisoners?
accepted.x: The Mulla Committee (1980–83) focused on all-India jail reforms, including a national prison policy, an All India Prison Service and separate undertrials.
accepted.tq: Match the committee’s period and broad reform agenda with its recommendations.
accepted.sec: Prison reform committees → focus (Mulla, Krishna Iyer, Justice Amitava Roy)

accepted.s: The Krishna Iyer Committee (1987) primarily focused on which of the following?
o: Death penalty for terrorism and waging war
UNCAT ratification and the PEACE model
Women prisoners and increasing the representation of women in the police
accepted.x: The Krishna Iyer Committee (1987) focused on women prisoners and the need for more women in the police.
accepted.tq: Identify the gender-related prison and policing focus of the committee.
accepted.sec: Prison reform committees → focus (Mulla, Krishna Iyer, Justice Amitava Roy)

accepted.s: The Justice Amitava Roy Committee, appointed by the Supreme Court in 2018, dealt primarily with which set of issues?
o: National prison policy, All India Prison Service and women in police
Overcrowding, undertrials, legal aid and speedy trial
Capital punishment, terrorism and waging war
accepted.x: The Supreme Court-appointed Justice Amitava Roy Committee (2018) focused on overcrowding, undertrials, legal aid and speedy trial.
accepted.tq: Use the committee’s appointment context and issue cluster to distinguish it from earlier committees.
accepted.sec: Prison reform committees → focus (Mulla, Krishna Iyer, Justice Amitava Roy)

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly matches the Law Commission report with its subject?
o: 262nd Report (2015) — abolition of the death penalty for all crimes except terrorism and waging war
273rd Report (2017) — classification of rarest-of-rare cases under Machhi Singh
262nd Report (2015) — ratification of UNCAT and draft Prevention of Torture Bill, 2017
273rd Report (2017) — creation of the All India Prison Service
accepted.x: The 262nd Report (2015) recommended abolishing the death penalty for all crimes except terrorism and waging war. The 273rd Report concerned UNCAT ratification and a draft anti-torture Bill.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between the two Law Commission reports by subject and year.
accepted.sec: Law Commission reports → subject (262nd, 273rd)

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the 262nd Law Commission Report:
1. It was submitted in 2015.
2. It recommended abolition of the death penalty for all crimes except terrorism and waging war.
3. It recommended retaining the death penalty for every offence involving violence.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The 262nd Report was issued in 2015 and recommended abolition of the death penalty except for terrorism and waging war. It did not recommend retention for every violent offence.
accepted.tq: Reject the broad retention claim that exceeds the stated exceptions.
accepted.sec: Law Commission reports → subject (262nd, 273rd)
